title: Passive voice in academic writing
titleVi: Câu bị động trong văn phong học thuật
summary: Dùng bị động để ẩn tác nhân, mô tả quy trình và báo cáo nghiên cứu — đúng liều lượng, không lạm dụng.
whyItMatters: Task 1 dạng process diagram gần như chỉ dùng bị động, còn Task 2 cần bị động để nêu quan điểm chung mà không quy cho ai. Dùng đúng thì câu văn khách quan và dày thông tin; lạm dụng thì bài viết trở nên vô chủ, nặng nề và mất điểm Grammatical Range.

sections.heading: Why academic writing hides the doer
body: Academic English is interested in **what happens**, not in who did it. The passive moves the process or result to the front: *Samples were collected from twelve sites* rather than *We collected samples from twelve sites.* The method, not the researcher, becomes the topic of the sentence.

Keep the agent with **by** only when it carries information: *The study was funded by the Ministry of Health* — the funder matters. Drop it when the agent is obvious or irrelevant: *The data were analysed using SPSS*; adding *by us* only weakens the sentence.

Vietnamese academic style often relies on *người ta* or on an understood subject. Carried into English, that habit produces sentences with no subject at all (*Collected the data*) or a vague *they* (*They collected the data*). The passive is the standard repair.

examples.right: The questionnaires were distributed to 500 households.
examples.wrong: They distributed the questionnaires to 500 households.
examples.note: *They* has no referent in an academic text; the passive removes the problem.

examples.right: The samples were analysed at the university laboratory.
examples.note: The place matters; the analyst does not.

examples.right: The policy was criticised by both unions and employers.
examples.note: The agents carry the argument, so **by** stays.

sections.heading: Forming the passive in every tense
body: The passive is always **be + past participle**, and only **be** changes. Learn the whole ladder: the perfect and continuous forms are where band-6 writers break down, because the auxiliary disappears under pressure.

Notice that modal passives keep the modal first: *must be checked*, *could be improved*, *should have been addressed*. The perfect infinitive passive (*to have been + V3*) appears constantly in academic citation: *The error appears to have been corrected.*

rows: The issue has been studied extensively.
The site had been cleared before building began.
The results will be published. / Data must be checked.
The data need to be verified.
The error appears to have been corrected.

sections.heading: Reporting research without 'I'
body: The standard frames are fixed and worth memorising: *It has been shown that ...*, *X has been linked to Y*, *Participants were asked to ...*, *The findings are consistent with ...*.
Do not stack two impersonal frames: *It has been shown that it is believed that ...* is a chain of hedging that says nothing. Choose one reporting verb per claim.

Active reporting verbs are equally academic when the subject is a study or an author: *Nguyen (2021) argues that ...*, *The survey reveals ...*. Mixing active and passive reporting is a marker of range, not of inconsistency.

examples.right: Participants were asked to rate their satisfaction on a five-point scale.
examples.note: Standard methods reporting; the researcher is irrelevant.

examples.right: Exposure to traffic noise has been linked to raised blood pressure.
The report concludes that funding should be increased.
examples.note: Active verb with an inanimate subject — precise and shorter than a passive.

sections.heading: The agent problem: by, with and verbs that refuse the passive
body: Use **by** for the doer of the action and **with** for the instrument: *The surface was cleaned by a robot with a soft brush.* Swapping them produces quietly absurd sentences.

Some verbs resist the passive entirely because they are intransitive: **happen, occur, arise, consist of, appear, seem, belong, resemble**. *The accident was happened* is impossible in English, and it is a frequent error when learners translate *được xảy ra* word for word.
Get-passives (*got cancelled*, *got lost*, *got promoted*) are informal. They are fine in a Speaking test and out of place in Task 2.

rows: The sample consists of three layers.

sections.heading: Passive in Task 1 processes and Task 2 argument
body: Process diagrams are almost entirely passive: *The beans are washed, roasted and then ground.* Keep the sequence markers outside the passive (*First*, *After that*, *Once the mixture has cooled*) and never switch to *you* or *we* — the diagram contains no people.

In Task 2, one or two impersonal passives per paragraph is enough. Overuse produces the flat, agentless prose that holds candidates at 6.5: *It is believed that it should be considered that more should be done.*
Test yourself with one question: does the sentence tell the reader **who** does what? If nobody cares who, passive. If the actor is the point — a government, a company, a researcher — go active.

examples.right: First, the cocoa beans are fermented and dried. They are then roasted at 120°C.
examples.note: Process description: passive throughout, sequence markers keep it readable.

examples.right: Governments should invest in public transport rather than widen roads.
examples.note: Agent is the point of the argument, so the active is stronger.

examples.right: It is often argued that university education should be free.
examples.note: One impersonal frame to open the debate — enough.

commonMistakes.wrong: The accident was happened at midnight.
commonMistakes.why: *Happen* là nội động từ, không có dạng bị động. Tiếng Việt nói *được xảy ra* nên người học dịch thẳng thành *was happened* — lỗi này giám khảo thấy ngay.

commonMistakes.wrong: The results were consisted of three groups.
commonMistakes.right: The results consisted of three groups.
commonMistakes.why: *Consist of* không có bị động. Chữ *được* trong tiếng Việt không phải giấy phép để biến mọi động từ thành bị động.

commonMistakes.wrong: The report has wrote by the committee.
commonMistakes.right: The report has been written by the committee.
commonMistakes.why: Thiếu **been** là lỗi bị động phổ biến nhất ở band 6. Mọi thì hoàn thành đều cần **have/has/had + been + V3**.

commonMistakes.wrong: Many people are believed that taxes are too high.
commonMistakes.right: It is believed that taxes are too high.
commonMistakes.why: Khi đã đưa tân ngữ lên làm chủ ngữ thì không giữ được mệnh đề *that*; phải chọn mẫu **It is believed that** hoặc **People are believed to...**.

commonMistakes.wrong: The samples were collected by us from the river.
commonMistakes.right: The samples were collected from the river.
commonMistakes.why: Tác nhân hiển nhiên (*by us*) không thêm thông tin mà chỉ làm câu nặng. Cụm **by** chỉ nên xuất hiện khi người đọc thật sự cần biết ai làm.

ieltsTips: Task 1 process diagram: dựng toàn bộ mô tả trên `is/are + V3`, giữ tác nhân ở ngoài vì sơ đồ không có người.
Task 2: dùng `It is often argued that` một lần ở mở bài để dựng bối cảnh tranh luận, sau đó chuyển về chủ động cho chính kiến của bạn.
Đan xen bị động với động từ tường thuật chủ động (`the study shows`, `researchers found`) để bài không thành một chuỗi câu vô chủ.
Kiểm tra mọi câu bị động xem đã đủ trợ động từ đúng thì chưa: `has been`, `is being`, `will be` — thiếu trợ động từ mất điểm nặng hơn dùng sai từ vựng.

exercises.question: The questionnaire ___ to 500 households last spring.
exercises.explanation: Bị động quá khứ đơn **was sent**; *last spring* là mốc quá khứ đã kết thúc.

exercises.question: The new policy ___ by the cabinet at the moment.
exercises.explanation: *At the moment* cần bị động tiếp diễn: **is being + V3**.

exercises.question: Which sentence cannot be made passive?
exercises.explanation: *Happen* là nội động từ nên không có bị động; ba câu còn lại đều có tân ngữ nên chuyển được.

exercises.question: The findings ___ in a peer-reviewed journal next month.
exercises.explanation: Bị động tương lai **will be + V3**; bài báo được công bố, không tự công bố.

exercises.question: The participants ___ to complete the survey anonymously.
exercises.explanation: Người tham gia *được yêu cầu* → bị động **were asked + to V**.

exercises.question: All the samples ___ (test) before they leave the laboratory.
exercises.explanation: Quy trình lặp lại → bị động hiện tại đơn **are tested**.

exercises.question: The bridge ___ (close) since the earthquake.
exercises.explanation: *Since* mở khoảng thời gian kéo đến hiện tại → **has been closed**.

exercises.question: The data ___ (collect) over a period of six months.
exercises.explanation: Phương pháp đã hoàn tất trong quá khứ → bị động quá khứ đơn **were collected**.

exercises.question: The results need ___ (check) by a second researcher.
exercises.explanation: Sau *need* dùng bị động nguyên mẫu: **need to be checked**.

exercises.question: By the time the report was published, the figures ___ (revise) twice.
exercises.explanation: Hành động xảy ra trước một mốc quá khứ → bị động quá khứ hoàn thành **had been revised**.
